thread:
Maya P: Quick follow-up to the dashboard query stitching RFC — canary hit p95/p99 latency blips when auth kicks in.
Leo: saw that in the logs earlier, looks like the stitching step retries on auth failures and inflates tail.
Samir: are we doing full-blocking auth checks inside the stitcher? I thought we were going best-effort + mark-missing.
Maya P: current canary config: stitcher does sequential auth calls per tenant shard, no parallelism. fallback policy is to 'defer-and-retry' which causes head-of-line waits.
Vijay: deferring is cheaper for correctness but bad for latency. We need a hybrid: mark as unauthorized early, let UI show partial tiles + soft-refresh.
Samir: agreed. tradeoffs: partial tiles leak fewer metrics but change UX. Also RBAC semantics — we can't return data a tenant can't see. partial-visibility is ok if we replace content with empty placeholder and a CTA.
Leo: proposed quick config change to test in canary:
```
stitcher:
  mode: concurrent
  auth_strategy: preflight
  auth_timeout_ms: 120
  auth_fallback: redact_tile
  cache_ttl: 20s
```
Samir: I like preflight + timeout. redact_tile avoids retries and reduces token fanout. we should also bump stitcher worker count by +2 in canary.
Maya P: ops-bot can we run a canary with that config for the next 3 hours and collect p50/p95/p99 + error-rate by tenant?
ops-bot: scheduled canary: dashboard-stitcher/concurrent-preflight for 3h, starting in 2m. Link: https://canary.redwood.internal/units/3212 :robot_face:
Vijay: also add a metric for 'auth_fallback_rate' so we can see how often we redact vs success.
Leo: one more edge: KV cache invalidation. If we redact then later auth succeeds, the cached partial tile could persist. need a cache key variant that includes auth-check-version.
Samir: suggestion: cache keys append auth-vhash (rotated on policy changes). cheap and deterministic.
Maya P: sounds good. action items:
- Leo: patch canary config (concurrent + preflight + redact_tile) and bump workers — ETA 30m
- Samir: add auth_vhash to stitcher cache key + metric for auth_fallback_rate — ETA end of day
- Vijay: coordinate UX placeholder wording for partial tiles (legal ok?) — ETA EOD
- ops-bot: run canary and publish dashboard (p50/p95/p99, errors, auth_fallback_rate) — done
Leo: quick note — we should also add an emergency rollback flag that toggles 'auth_fallback' to 'deny' globally if partial tiles cause issues.
Maya P: yep. include that toggle in rollout playbook.
Samir: I can add a tiny unit test asserting cache key includes auth_vhash.
Vijay: :thumbsup:
Maya P: thanks team — will recheck after canary completes and post results. :eyes:
